STEP 1 - Scene: A small side salad of mixed leafy greens (red and green lettuce leaves) with shredded carrot and a few bits of garlic or onion, on a white square plate. Photographed from above, nearly top-down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 26 cm across at its widest edge. Treating it as a dinner-size plate, area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2. The salad occupies only the right-hand portion of the plate.

STEP 3 - Items: (1) mixed leafy greens (green and red-tinged lettuce, some dark leaves), (2) shredded carrot, (3) a few small pale bits (garlic or onion slivers). No visible dressing pool or oil sheen.

STEP 4 - Area: Greens cover about 12% of the plate (~64 cm^2), carrot shreds about 1% (~5 cm^2), garlic/onion bits about 0.5% (~3 cm^2). Total food coverage ≈ 13.5% (~72 cm^2).

STEP 5 - Volume: Greens 64 cm^2 x 2.5 cm ≈ 160 ml (loosely piled). Carrot 5 cm^2 x 0.5 cm ≈ 2.5 ml. Garlic/onion ≈ 1 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Greens 160 ml x 0.15 ≈ 24 g. Carrot 2.5 ml x 0.6 ≈ 1.5 g. Garlic/onion 1 ml x 0.6 ≈ 0.6 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Leafy greens ~20 kcal/100 g → 24 g ≈ 5 kcal. Carrot ~40 kcal/100 g → 1.5 g ≈ 0.6 kcal. Garlic/onion ~40 kcal/100 g → 0.6 g ≈ 0.2 kcal. Total ≈ 6 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A small handful of greens with a few carrot shreds on a large plate is plausible at roughly 25 g and single-digit kcal. Since no dressing is visible, the energy stays low; a dressed salad would add considerably more.
